result.title: Monte Carlo Random Walk Kernel
result.summary: We introduce the Monte Carlo Random Walk Kernel (MCRWK), an estimator whose per-pair cost is independent of graph size and derived directly from the random walk kernel (RWK) expansion. By normalizing the kernel coefficients, MCRWK samples a shared walk length and estimates its contribution using random walks on the input graphs. This gives a simple way to approximate RWK without constructing the product graph. For a fixed expected walk length and efficient neighbor sampling, each pairwise estimate takes $O(m)$ time for $m$ Monte Carlo samples, allowing the sample budget to control the trade-off between runtime and accuracy. We evaluate MCRWK against Graph Voyagers and classical RWK methods on synthetic and real graph datasets. In the reported experiments on large synthetic graphs, MCRWK is faster than Graph Voyagers and, at matched runtime, more accurate. It also has the lowest Gram-matrix runtime on the five real datasets studied. Code and experiments are available at https://github.com/arslan-yam/random_walk_kernels_computations

AI.brief_summary: 提出 Monte Carlo Random Walk Kernel（MCRWK），由随机游走核的展开式导出，采样共享游走长度并用图上游走估计其贡献，从而无需构造乘积图即可近似 RWK，单对样本成本 $O(m)$ 与图规模无关，并在合成与真实图上与 Graph Voyagers 及经典 RWK 比较。
AI.relevance_reason: 以采样预算显式权衡相似度估计的精度与运行成本，可能为 latent 推理轨迹或状态结构之间的相似度/对应关系评估提供一种低成本近似思路，其方差与可迁移性可供核查。
